message.content:
Let the reflection be across a line through the origin making angle \(\theta\) with the \(x\)-axis. Its matrix is

\[
R=\begin{pmatrix}
\cos 2\theta & \sin 2\theta\\
\sin 2\theta & -\cos 2\theta
\end{pmatrix}.
\]

Since

\[
R\begin{pmatrix}5\\0\end{pmatrix}
=
\begin{pmatrix}4\\3\end{pmatrix},
\]

we get

\[
5\begin{pmatrix}\cos 2\theta\\ \sin 2\theta\end{pmatrix}
=
\begin{pmatrix}4\\3\end{pmatrix},
\]

so

\[
\cos 2\theta=\frac45,\qquad \sin 2\theta=\frac35.
\]

Thus

\[
R=\begin{pmatrix}
\frac45 & \frac35\\
\frac35 & -\frac45
\end{pmatrix}.
\]

Now apply \(R\) to \(\begin{pmatrix}-2\\3\end{pmatrix}\):

\[
R\begin{pmatrix}-2\\3\end{pmatrix}
=
\begin{pmatrix}
\frac45(-2)+\frac35(3)\\[2mm]
\frac35(-2)-\frac45(3)
\end{pmatrix}
=
\begin{pmatrix}
\frac{-8+9}{5}\\[2mm]
\frac{-6-12}{5}
\end{pmatrix}
=
\begin{pmatrix}
\frac15\\[2mm]
-\frac{18}{5}
\end{pmatrix}.
\]

The answer is \(\begin{pmatrix}\frac15\\-\frac{18}{5}\end{pmatrix}\).
